items.note: Directly answers: Pro churn rose sharply after July (1 cancellation before August vs 10 in Aug–Sep), but causation by the price increase can't be established from this data.
Excludes the 5 @ourco.test accounts, leaving 40 accounts (20 Pro, 20 Basic). That count is correct.
Counts an account as churned when cancel_month is present. Its 11 Pro cancellations match the data.
Not written for a CEO: long and technical (account-months at risk, censoring, circular price-field reasoning, alternative July definitions, a data wishlist).
Far exceeds 5 bullets: about 13 top-level bullets across three sections, plus many sub-bullets.
Suggests one chart: monthly Pro vs Basic churn rate, with a July marker and the at-risk count labelled at each point.
States confidence per claim and explains it: fairly confident churn rose, low to moderate confidence the price increase caused it, given only 20 Pro accounts and 11 cancellations.
